thread:
maya (support): Hey team, ACME reported their console hourly usage stopped updating ~5 hours ago. Last visible hourly row is 03:00 UTC. They see no errors in UI, just empty bars since 04:00.

emily (customer-success): putting customer on hold, asked for org id and scope. They sent org_id=acme-enterprises and a screenshot.

maya (support): thx, forwarded. Can infra look for ETL/backfill issues for that org?

jonathan (eng-infra): looking. consumer group `usage-hourly-consumer` shows a lag spike at 04:05 UTC, then a restart at 04:12 UTC. offsets jumped back ~6 hours. Possible rebalancing.

samir (ingest): @jonathan can you paste the consumer lag output?

jonathan (eng-infra): here —

```
TOPIC                       PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
usage_hourly_rollups         12         1245123         1245123         0
usage_hourly_rollups         13         1241000         1247000         6000
usage_hourly_rollups         14         1243000         1243000         0
```

jonathan (eng-infra): partition 13 shows ~6k lag corresponding to ~5 hours of data. consumer restarted and didn't catch up due to backpressure on worker.

maya (support): is this limited to ACME or tenant-agnostic?

samir (ingest): looks cross-tenant but ACME hits that partition more. root cause: one ETL task OOM+retry loop after the restart, it throttled rehydration queue.

dave (oncall): on it — increasing concurrency for the requeue worker temporarily and bumping max processing threads. will watch.

ingest-bot: alert -> requeue-queue-depth: 12k (threshold 1000)

jonathan (eng-infra): i'm manually triggering a consumer rebalance and a targeted backfill for partition 13. command: `k run job-backfill --env=prod --partition=13 --since=2026-03-17T04:00:00Z`

samir (ingest): also enabling prefix-caching bypass for the job to reduce per-record compute. should speed things up.

maya (support): updated customer: "we're seeing a transient ingest backlog, team is running a targeted backfill and will monitor. expect visibility restored in 1-2 hours." they replied :ok_hand:.

dave (oncall): requeue depth dropping now 12k -> 4.2k. consumer lag 6000 -> 2100.

jonathan (eng-infra): backfill job logs: `processed 3200 records/min` — projection ~40m to clear remaining backlog if sustained.

emily (customer-success): told ACME ETA ~45m. asked if there will be any data loss.

samir (ingest): no data loss, just delayed. once offsets caught up, hourly rollups will backfill. we'll push a small dashboard note about delayed metrics.

maya (support): sweet. flagging as P2 incident for tracking. will close thread when console shows new hourly rows for ACME.

ingest-bot: info -> backfill-job-5187654321 finished: processed=240000, duration=35m, errors=0

jonathan (eng-infra): offsets fully caught up at 05:05 UTC. I can see new hourly rows ingested for acme-enterprises (05:00, 06:00).

maya (support): confirmed with customer, they see the missing hours restored. closing. thanks all :heart:
